study_type.claude: Qualitative-Interviews (39 semi-structured interviews, reflexive thematic analysis)

research_method.claude: 39 audio-recorded semi-structured Zoom interviews analysed by reflexive thematic analysis (Braun and Clarke), no IRR; 30 interviews from a prior DIY-tools study plus 9 new, 5 re-interviewed; non-probabilistic recruitment (networks, mailing lists, snowball)
research_method.nlm: Semi-structured interviews with reflexive thematic analysis, no IRR; 39 BLVSPs; non-probabilistic recruitment (networks, mailing lists, snowball)
research_method.value: Semi-structured, audio-recorded Zoom interviews with 39 blind and low vision software professionals (30 from a prior DIY-tools study, 9 new, 5 re-interviewed), analysed with reflexive thematic analysis (Braun and Clarke) without IRR; non-probabilistic recruitment via professional networks, mailing lists and snowball sampling
research_method.note: Two interview waves and re-interviews reported only by Claude (not contradicted).

context.claude: Industry; BLVSPs in corporate settings (startups to multinationals) or freelancing, several countries (67% North America); 39 participants, 21 software engineers
context.nlm: Industry and freelance; startups to multinationals; 39 BLVSPs (67% North America), software engineers n=21, accessibility specialists n=5
context.value: industry; blind and low vision software professionals in corporate settings (startups to multinationals) or freelancing, mainly North America (67%); 39 participants (21 software engineers, 5 accessibility specialists, others)

ai_discussed.note: GenAI use at work by BLV software professionals is the topic.

remote_covid.note: Work mode not specified by either; remote meetings appear only in related work.

data_window.claude: May–July 2024 (30 interviews) and January–February 2025 (9 new interviews)
data_window.note: Claude: May–July 2024 and January–February 2025. NotebookLM gives no period. Full text confirms Claude's dates (PDF p. 3).

cat_productivity.note: Borderline: only perceived productivity gains from interviews (assigned to Survey by the ficha); no productivity metric.

cat_quality.note: Only one participant's confidence (80–90%) in GenAI visual descriptions; hallucinations discussed as a risk, no quality metric.

cat_collaboration.note: Borderline: themes 'Less reliance on sighted colleagues', 'Better participation in professional conversations' and the verification catch-22 (needing colleagues to verify); no collaboration metric.

cat_satisfaction.note: Theme 'Productivity gains and well-being': reduced stress and mental toll (self-reported).

cat_activity.note: Both tag self-reported GenAI usage frequency (and NotebookLM access labor) as Activity; not repository activity.

cat_devex.note: NotebookLM tags several items 'DevEx'; the DevEx framework is not referenced.

cat_survey.note: Interviews about perceptions; all measures are self-reported.

evidence.quote: We conducted audio-recorded, semi-structured interviews with 39 BLVSPs over Zoom.
reflexive thematic analysis considers researcher subjectivity and interpretation as valuable analytical resources [13]. Therefore, we did not calculate IRR.

30 participants were interviewed as part of the prior study on DIY tools [18], between May 2024 and July 2024. 9 additional participants were recruited specifically for this study on the use of GenAI at work, interviewed between January 2025 and February 2025.
are working or have worked in a software development position either in a corporate setting or as a freelancer, and have at least one year of work experience.
Company sizes also varied, from startups to multinational corporations.
RQ1. How do BLVSPs perceive and utilize generative AI in the workplace?
BLVSPs reported substantial improvements in their work efficiency and stress levels after using GenAI: "I'm faster and I use less resources. I'm not as stressed" (P10).
4.2.2 Less Reliance on Sighted Colleagues. Despite needing sighted assistance at times, participants felt uneasy burdening their colleagues.
Thus, participants perceived GenAI as "the colleague that doesn't get annoyed at me" (P7)
